First listed: 2026-04-24 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Is a Recession Coming? What 100+ Companies Are Telling Us | The Weekly Wrap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uii5YCeMhEI) - 2026-04-24
- [Substack: Is a Recession Coming? What 100+ Companies Are Telling Us | The Weekly Wrap](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/is-a-recession-coming-what-100-companies-78e) - 2026-04-24

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman finds no imminent recession in broad earnings and credit data, favors AI-related industrials, and treats health-insurer rebounds and software bottom-fishing cautiously. His debt discussion combines a defensible Treasury-demand argument with an incorrect repo-collateral exclusivity claim. A detailed viewer letter challenges simple AI-disruption narratives; Eisman partially accepts incumbent survival while retaining a bearish seat-and-pricing thesis. The disagreement over stock compensation concerns economic cost versus accounting measurement and should not be reduced to opposing factual claims.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 026. Stock compensation is a real economic expense and should not be ignored merely because adjusted earnings add it back.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 29:29-29:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uii5YCeMhEI&t=1769s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Qualification: The viewer agreed that dilution matters; Eisman's rebuttal does not actually refute the grant-date accounting point.

Conditional reasoning: Compensation transfers an economic claim to employees. A noncash settlement changes financing, not whether labor consumes value. Tax deductibility timing and grant-date expense are separate issues.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.


## Framework and tools

- Manager earnings and investor fund returns are different measures.
- Require operating evidence before accepting a turnaround.
- Distinguish software coding cost from maintenance, sales and compliance.
- Separate accounting measurement from economic dilution.
- Use market prices as evidence, not proof that a risk cannot exist.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- BCRED marks, nonaccruals and inflows.
- Health-insurer medical loss ratios and enrollment.
- GE Vernova orders and forward valuation.
- Treasury yields and debt/GDP.
- Software total cost of ownership and stock-compensation example.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman delivers a solo monologue; inserted advertisements and opening montage are excluded.
- Every segment read; truncated display section was reread in full.
- Boris's views are separately attributed and excluded from Eisman forecast scoring.
- The claim that repo accepts only short Treasuries is distinct from the broader Treasury-demand thesis.
